title: Uruk grows into a large city
summary: Around 3200 BCE, Uruk in southern Mesopotamia contained large monumental buildings and a substantial urban population. Administrative practices developed within this increasingly complex settlement.

citations.note: Supports the factual summary and chronology. Context includes explicitly interpretive comparisons; the date note identifies limits of precision.

claims.text: Around 3200 BCE, Uruk in southern Mesopotamia contained large monumental buildings and a substantial urban population. Administrative practices developed within this increasingly complex settlement.
Approximate urban development milestone; no exact foundation date.
The city is a useful case for comparing urbanization with the Indus region and the Andes. Such comparison does not establish that every city arose through the same institutions.
